newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN, NATO probe arrest of 28 foreigners in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: UN, NATO probe arrest of 28 foreigners in Bosnia.

text.p: Peacekeeping forces are investigating the detention of 24 Iraqis and four Jordanians by Bosnian authorities who accuse them of entering the country illegally, IFOR officials said.

Alex Ivanko, a spokesman for the International Police Task Force (IPTF), said 30 foreign civilians arrived on a Jordanian military flight at Sarajevo airport on Sunday and were allowed to enter the country without the usual checks.
"(The U.N.) witnessed them disembarking and they were allowed by French soldiers to proceed without passport or customs control," Ivanko said.
French troops serving in the NATO-led peace force (IFOR) help control the movement of military flights and their passengers through the airport.
U.N. police could not confirm the nationality of the civilians and said the group left the airport on a public bus.
Ivanko said local Bosnian police detained 28 of the 30 for "illegal entry to the country". It was not imediately clear what happened to the other two.
Ivanko said all 28 foreigners were in Bosnian police detention, although it is not clear what the Bosnian authorities intend doing with them.
IFOR said it was still reviewing the incident.
"This is all very strange," said an IFOR officer who asked not to be named. "It is extraordinary that this has happened.
"In theory people should not be let through like this (without passport checks)."
A U.N. official who witnessed the event wrote a report which quoted French military police as saying the group were refugees and that Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation police would deal with them.

"The current system, with military aircraft transporting civilian passengers and allowing them to disembark in areas restricted to federation police, and not to be processed through passport and customs inpsection, has high potential for criminal activity," the U.N. report said.
NATO said earlier an IFOR flight on September 29 brought 30 Jordanian troops to Bosnia who are serving in the peace force.
Jordan has some 60 troops deployed in the Sarajevo area as part of the IFOR contingent.

"We still do not know who they are, but it's pretty obvious that they did arrive on an IFOR-Jordanian flight to Sarajevo and it is likely that we will be asked to help deport them," said the IFOR officer.
